newsitem.title: USA: HP to unveil encryption breakthrough.
newsitem.headline: HP to unveil encryption breakthrough.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. said Friday that it will unveil a breakthrough agreement on Monday in the long-deadlocked debate over software encryption, a development that could eliminate a key impediment to the growth of electronic commerce via the Internet.

A spokesman said H-P Chairman and Chief Executive Lewis Platt will provide details of a deal involving computer industry leaders, the Clinton administation and other governments at a press conference in Washington.

The company confirmed that the technology will enable export of strong encryption capabilities, such as those that companies want to use for tasks ranging from confidential communications to electronic commerce.
"It involves a framework for secure electronic commerce and internet transactions," a Hewlett-Packard spokesman said of the technology.

Encryption programmes use mathematical formulas to scramble information, such as electronic mail messages or a credit card numbers, to render them unreadable to computer users without a password or "software key" that can unlock the coded material.
Under existing national security laws dating from the Cold War era, the U.S. government has allowed the export of software only with weak data encryption.
Encryption has been classified as a munition because of its potential for use by terrorists, spies or other criminals.
For years the U.S. computer industry has complained that such restrictions have hampered its products' competitiveness in world markets.

In addition, the industry says the laws have prevented it from offering some of the most recent Internet technologies, even within the United States, because it is impossible to prevent computer users outside U.S. borders from gaining access to the technology once it is publicly available on the Internet.
Executives from microprocessor giant Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp. will also speak at the Monday briefing at the National Press Club.
